data.turoyo: Rġiz Aloho aʕlayye, raḥəq mə foṯox w mad dəkoṯani, d manḥət nuro, kabrit xəd zlum-ʕamur aʕlayye.
data.translation: God grew angry with them, far from your face and from these places, to send down fire and sulphur upon them, like Sodom and Gomorrah.

rationale: Detransitive Preterit sense 1 has one example; explicit divine experiencer and ʕal-marked persons add argument-coding evidence.

summary: Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. Supplied English is project machine translation, retained verbatim where quoted; semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo.
Rġiz matches the inherited rġīz Detransitive Preterit; no active stem, new box or anger sense is required.
The target aʕlayye is distinct from the harmful deed/cause in the inherited quotation. Do not reduce the difference to free m-/ʕal alternation without controlling participant roles.
Religious comparison and the protective expression raḥəq mə foṯox remain in the quoted context; neither is a new fixed idiom of rġz.
Can m- and ʕal mark the same anger participant, or does m- primarily introduce cause and ʕal the target? This two-example sample cannot decide.

Detransitive anger has a subject experiencer Aloho and aʕlayye as its personal target. Existing example has ʕal-marked deed and mene; the difference is participant role, not automatically competing government for the same argument.
